title: Young Adulthood: Harb al-Fijar, Hilf al-Fudul, and Marriage to Khadijah
overview: This episode covers key events in the young adult life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ prior to revelation, including his participation in Harb al-Fijar and his endorsement of Hilf al-Fudul to protect the oppressed. It further details his trade expedition to Sham on behalf of Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, where his exceptional character, honesty, and business skill were witnessed by Maysarah. The episode concludes with the proposal and marriage of Muhammad ﷺ to Khadijah at age twenty-five.
lessons: Allah prepares His chosen servants through life experiences (tarbiyah), building empathy for orphans, the poor, and the downtrodden.
True nobility lies in standing up for the oppressed and enforcing justice regardless of social status, wealth, or power.
Islam upholds and ratifies noble principles and pacts of justice established even before Islamic revelation.
Honesty, integrity, and trustworthiness (being al-Sadiq al-Amin) build a lasting reputation that opens doors in both business and personal life.
Character, moral integrity, and pious compatibility are the most vital qualities to seek in a marriage partner.

chapters.title: Return to Makkah and Early Upbringing
chapters.summary: The lecture begins with a brief recap of the Prophet's ﷺ journey to Sham at age twelve, where the monk Buhayra recognized signs of prophethood and advised Abu Talib to send him back to Makkah for protection. Growing up in Makkah, young Muhammad ﷺ was protected by Allah from all bad behavior and evil customs of Jahiliyyah. He developed the highest moral standards, sincerity, and complete truthfulness. These early years served as divine preparation (tarbiyah) for his future role as Allah's Messenger.
key_points: Recap of the encounter with the Christian monk Buhayra at age twelve
Advice to return to Makkah to protect Muhammad ﷺ from potential harm
Divine protection (tarbiyah) keeping Muhammad ﷺ away from Jahiliyyah vices
Development of flawless character, honesty, and truthfulness

chapters.title: Harb al-Fijar (The Sacrilegious War)
chapters.summary: At around twenty years of age, the Prophet ﷺ witnessed Harb al-Fijar, a sacrilegious war between Hawazin and Quraysh. The conflict received its name because Hawazin violated the sacred months (Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and Muharram) by launching an unexpected attack against Quraysh. Although Muhammad ﷺ did not engage directly in hand-to-hand combat, he assisted his uncles on the battlefield by handing them arrows. This gave him early firsthand experience of battle tactics and leadership under divine decree.
key_points: Harb al-Fijar occurred when Muhammad ﷺ was approximately twenty years old
Conflict between the Hawazin tribe and Quraysh inside the sacred months
The four sacred months: Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and Muharram
Muhammad ﷺ aided his uncles by handing them arrows during the battle
Battlefield exposure served as practical training for future military leadership

chapters.title: Hilf al-Fudul: The Cause and the Oath
chapters.summary: Shortly after Harb al-Fijar, a prominent Makkan leader named al-As ibn Wa'il refused to pay a poor Yemeni merchant for his goods. Denied justice, the merchant went to Dar al-Nadwah and threatened to publicize Qurayshi commercial dishonor across all Arab tribes. Fearing damage to their trading reputation, three Makkan leaders named al-Fadl formed Hilf al-Fudul (The Alliance of the Virtuous). They swore an oath to fight any oppressor in Makkah until justice was restored. Young Muhammad ﷺ proudly joined this pact.
key_points: Al-As ibn Wa'il cheated a poor Yemeni trader of his payment
The merchant appealed at Dar al-Nadwah, threatening to expose Qurayshi dishonesty
Three leaders named al-Fadl initiated the alliance, naming it Hilf al-Fudul
Pact members swore to defend anyone wronged in Makkah regardless of status or wealth
Muhammad ﷺ joined the alliance as a young man and praised its noble principles

chapters.title: Enforcing the Oath and Its Islamic Legacy
chapters.summary: Armed with swords, the alliance members confronted al-As ibn Wa'il at his home and forced him to pay the Yemeni merchant immediately. The principles of Hilf al-Fudul aligned so closely with Islamic values of justice that the alliance remained active through the era of the Sahabah, the Khulafa al-Rashidin, and the Umayyad period. Decades later, al-Husayn ibn Ali threatened to invoke Hilf al-Fudul against an unjust governor in Madinah, and Abdullah ibn Zubayr pledged to enforce it with his sword.
key_points: Alliance members confronted al-As ibn Wa'il with drawn swords to enforce justice
Hilf al-Fudul was maintained and honored after the advent of Islam
Al-Husayn threatened to invoke Hilf al-Fudul against governor Al-Walid in Madinah
Abdullah ibn Zubayr swore to draw his sword to uphold the principles of Hilf al-Fudul

chapters.title: Trade Journey to Sham for Khadijah
chapters.summary: At twenty-five, Muhammad ﷺ was hired by Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, a wealthy and honorable Qurayshi noblewoman, to manage a trading caravan to Sham. Known throughout Makkah as al-Sadiq al-Amin, he was accompanied by Khadijah's servant Maysarah. During the trip, Maysarah witnessed remarkable events, including a cloud shading Muhammad ﷺ and a monk at a monastery identifying him as a prophet after he rested under a specific tree.
key_points: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid was a wealthy, highly respected twice-widowed noblewoman
Hired Muhammad ﷺ due to his legendary reputation as al-Sadiq al-Amin
Maysarah accompanied Muhammad ﷺ to assist him on his first trade trip to Sham
A cloud miraculously shaded Muhammad ﷺ throughout the journey
A Christian monk stated that only a prophet rests under that specific monastery tree

chapters.title: Unprecedented Business Success and Marriage Proposal
chapters.summary: Muhammad ﷺ demonstrated outstanding business intelligence by selling goods in Sham and buying local items to sell upon return to Makkah, bringing back unprecedented profits for Khadijah. Deeply moved by the high returns and Maysarah's glowing account of his humility, honesty, and noble character, Khadijah desired to marry him. She sent her friend Nafisah to inquire whether Muhammad ﷺ would accept. He agreed, leading to a highly successful and blessed marriage at the age of twenty-five.
key_points: Muhammad ﷺ generated double profits by trading both in Sham and upon return to Makkah
Maysarah reported Muhammad's ﷺ exceptional humility, honesty, and kindness
Khadijah expressed her interest in marriage through her friend Nafisah
Muhammad ﷺ accepted the proposal despite his modest wealth
The marriage took place when Muhammad ﷺ was twenty-five and Khadijah was forty

segments.ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ، وَصَلَّى اللَّهُ وَسَلَّمَ وَبَارَكَ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ
segments.translit: Alhamdu lillahi rabbil-alamin, wa sallallahu wa sallama wa baraka ala nabiyyina Muhammadin wa ala alihi wa sahbihi ajmain.

segments.ar: اللَّهُمَّ عَلِّمْنَا مَا يَنْفَعُنَا وَانْفَعْنَا بِمَا عَلَّمْتَنَا وَزِدْنَا عِلْمًا
segments.translit: Allahumma allimna ma yanfa'una wanfa'na bima allamtana wa zidna ilma.

segments.text: Last week we spoke about the childhood of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] and the years that he spent with his uncle [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]].

And we spoke about the expedition of [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] towards [[Sham|شَام]], towards the greater Syria area, and how [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] as a twelve-year-old boy accompanied him on part of that journey.
But he did not complete the journey, and we spoke about that story last week about the encounter that they had with the Christian monk [[Buhayra|بَحِيرَى]].

And how [[Buhayra|بَحِيرَى]] saw the signs of prophethood on the Prophet [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] even though he was a young boy—he was only twelve years old at the time.

And then [[Buhayra|بَحِيرَى]] advised [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] not to allow [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] to accompany the rest of the caravan to [[Sham|شَام]] because he said,
there are Jews in that place who will see this boy and they will recognize him just as I recognized him.
And they will know that he is the one who was prophesied in the previous scriptures, in the previous revelations.
But once they realize that he is not from [[Bani Isra'il|بَنِي إِسْرَائِيل]], once they realize that he is not from the progeny of [[Ya'qub|يَعْقُوب]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]],
rather he is from [[Bani Ismail|بَنِي إِسْمَاعِيل]], from the progeny of [[Ismail|إِسْمَاعِيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]], they will be jealous and they will kill him.
"So don't take him to [[Sham|شَام]], send him back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]." So he was sent back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So this happened when he was around twelve years old. So he lived in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], he continued to live there with his uncle, and he grew up in a very honorable way.
Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] protected him, even in his childhood, from any type of bad behavior.
Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] did not allow [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] even to witness any type of bad behavior.
And he grew up with the best character and the best morals, and he grew up with complete honesty, and complete truthfulness, and complete sincerity.
So he combined all the good characteristics that a person could have, even in his childhood.
So when he grew up to be a little bit older—he was about twenty years old, young man—a very important event took place in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
A great event took place in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] when the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] was about twenty years old.
And this event is known as [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]], [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]].
And the reason why it was called [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]]—we'll get to the reasoning behind that in a minute [[insha'Allah|إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ]].
The word [[al-Fijar|الْفِجَار]], it comes from [[al-Fijar|الْفُجُور]], and [[al-Fijar|فُجُور]] means to do something evil, to do something that is wrong.
So this is where this war got its name from, [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]].
And who is the one who did something wrong, who started this war? We'll get into that in a minute [[insha'Allah|إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ]].
So basically this war, it was between a tribe called [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]], which was a tribe from outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and between the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
And the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], of course, were from inside [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. So this war was between [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]] and [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].

Now we know that there are four months that are considered the sacred months: those are the months of [[Rajab|رَجَب]], [[Dhu al-Qa'dah|ذُو الْقَعْدَة]], [[Dhu al-Hijjah|ذُو الْحِجَّة]], and [[Muharram|مُحَرَّم]].
These are [[al-Ashhur al-Hurum|الأَشْهُرُ الْحُرُم]], the sacred months.
And they were made sacred by Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] when He created the heavens and the earth.

Before the creation of mankind, when Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] created the heavens and the earth, He made these four months sacred: [[Rajab|رَجَب]], [[Dhu al-Qa'dah|ذُو الْقَعْدَة]], [[Dhu al-Hijjah|ذُو الْحِجَّة]], and [[Muharram|مُحَرَّم]].
So what does it mean, these months are sacred? It means it is not permissible to start fighting, to start a war during these four months.
But if someone starts a war with you, then you are allowed, of course, to defend yourself.

So the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they respected this. And remember, the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] originally, the Arabs beforehand, they were on the religion of [[Ibrahim|إِبْرَاهِيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]].
But as we spoke about earlier, [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عَمْرُو بْنُ لُحَيّ]], he brought idol worship back into the Arabian Peninsula, so the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they were idol worshippers,
but they had still some remnants of the religion of [[Ibrahim|إِبْرَاهِيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]] still with them.

Even though their [[tawhid|تَوْحِيد]] was not there—they used to worship idols—they still had some pieces of the religion of [[Ibrahim|إِبْرَاهِيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]] with them that they used to observe.
For example, [[Hajj|حَجّ]] still used to take place.
And also [[al-Ashhur al-Hurum|الأَشْهُرُ الْحُرُم]], these four sacred months were still considered sacred by the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
So they would not even think about starting any fighting or starting any war at this time.
They considered it something that was impermissible, and they considered it something that was out of the question—they would never even think of starting a war at that time.
It was such to the extent that if somebody had murdered another person's father and then they went into hiding,
and when the [[al-Ashhur al-Hurum|الأَشْهُرُ الْحُرُم]] came—when these four sacred months came—if this man who murdered another person's father,
if he came out of hiding and the son of the murdered person saw the murderer of his father, he would not even touch him.
"Oh no, we can't do it. These are the four holy months, we cannot do anything in this time."
So they respected it to that extent, that they would not even touch the murderer of their own father if they happened to see him during this time.
But the tribe of [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]], they decided that they would take advantage of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]'s respect for these sacred months.

They thought to themselves, "Look, the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], during these four months, they're never even going to think about starting a fight, and they would not expect anyone else from the Arabs to fight them as well."
"They think that we all think like them.
Because they consider it sacred, they probably assume that all of the other Arabs, they will consider it sacred as well and they will respect that as well."
So the [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]], they decided to take advantage of this.
So they attacked the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] during [[al-Ashhur al-Hurum|الأَشْهُرُ الْحُرُم]], during the sacred months.
And the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they were not expecting this. It came totally out of the blue. It came to them as a surprise attack, so they were attacked.
And that is why it is called [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]].
As we said, [[al-Fijar|الْفِجَار]], it comes from [[al-Fijar|فُجُور]], meaning to commit an act of evil.
And who is the one who committed the act of evil? [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]], the tribe of [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]], for starting an act of aggression, starting a war during the sacred months.
This is an act of [[al-Fijar|فُجُور]], this is an act of evil.
And that is why these wars became known as [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]].
And it happened in the history of the Arabs five times. There were five instances of [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]].
And one of them happened during the time that the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] was about twenty years old.
So this is still about twenty years before he receives the first revelation—he's a young man.
So [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]], they attack [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], and of course [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they are defending themselves.
So the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] witnessed this battle with his own eyes, and he participated with the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] to some extent.
He didn't actually fight, he didn't actually fight, but he would give the arrows to his uncles.
The uncles of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], they were fighting, and the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] was right there in the middle of the battlefield,
and he would give the arrows to his uncles for his uncles to shoot.
So this was the extent of the participation of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] in the defense of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] in [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]].

So as we mentioned before, everything that happened in the life of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], it happened for some wisdom that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] decreed.
And it was preparing him for something that would happen in the future, like the fact that the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] grew up as an orphan—he was an orphan, right?
This prepared him later on in his life to show love and...
compassion to the orphans because he knew exactly what it's like to be an orphan.
The Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] grew up in poverty. He lived a life of poverty from his childhood,
so that he would understand what the people who are poor are going through, and he could deal with them on that type of a basis.
So every incident that happened in the life of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], it was a form of [[tarbiyah|تربية]] from Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] Himself.
It was a form of upbringing that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] caused the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] to go through,
so that he would be able to handle every situation with any type of person in the most perfect way.
So Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] is preparing him.
And battle is one of the things, of course, that the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], later on in his life, he would be the commander of the military of the Muslims,
and he would be very successful in that role as well.

So Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], from the young age of [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] is showing him how these things work.

So even though in [[Harb al-Fijar|حرب الفجار]] the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] didn't participate in terms of actually fighting, but he was right there in the middle of what was happening.
He was giving the arrows to his uncles who were fighting.
So he got a first-hand experience of what it's like to be in a battle,
and what it's like to be in the middle of a war, and how it works.
So this was an important event that took place in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] when the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] was about 20 years old.
Also around this time, another great event happened in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And this, again, was during the young adult life of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]],
before his marriage to [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]]. So he was in around his 20s, early 20s.
This event that happened in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] is known as [[Hilf al-Fudul|حلف الفضول]].
[[Hilf al-Fudul|حلف الفضول]]. And what is the background of [[Hilf al-Fudul|حلف الفضول]]?
There was a [[Yemen|يمني]] man who came for [[Hajj|حج]].
And the people, when they would come for [[Hajj|حج]], they would come for the pilgrimage, of course, but they would also use this as an opportunity to do business in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] as well.
And there's nothing wrong with this. A person who goes for [[Hajj|حج]] and he finds an opportunity to do some business as well, he does some business as well.
So this is what many of the people who would come to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] for [[Hajj|حج]], if they had some opportunity to do trade, they would do that.
So a [[Yemen|يمني]] man, poor [[Yemen|يمني]] man,
you know, a small-time businessman, he came for [[Hajj|حج]], and while he was there, he decided to do some business.
So he had some goods with him, and he sold them to a VIP of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]],
a leader from the leaders of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] whose name was [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص بن وائل]].
[[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص بن وائل]]. [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص بن وائل]], he was considered a very important person in the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], and he was wealthy, and he was powerful.
So this [[Yemen|يمني]] man, he sold his goods to [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص بن وائل]],
and [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص بن وائل]] told him, 'Okay, I'll pay you for it tomorrow. Come back tomorrow and I'll pay you for it.'
So the [[Yemen|يمني]] man said, 'Okay, no problem,' and he came back the next day.
And then [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص]] said to him again, 'Yeah, yeah, come back later. I'm not going to pay you right now.'
So the poor man said, 'Okay.' And this kept going on for a long, long time.
He kept asking for his payment, and [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص]] kept telling him to come back later, come back later, come back later, even though
[[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص]] was a very rich man,
and this [[Yemen|يمني]] man, he was not rich at all, and he needed this money.
So this went on for a long time.

He kept telling him, 'Come back, come back, come back,' until one day, finally, [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص]] got sick of this [[Yemen|يمني]] man coming to him all the time, and he said, 'Forget about it.
I'm not going to pay you anything. Just leave. Get out of my face.'
And [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص]], out of his arrogance, he thought that, 'What is anyone going to do to me? I'm this big VIP of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], I'm from the leaders of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
This [[Yemen|يمني]] guy is insignificant, he's a nobody, he's a poor guy. Nobody's going to stand up for him, and nobody can do anything to me.
What if I don't pay him his money? What's going to happen?'
So he told the [[Yemen|يمني]] man to leave him alone, and he said, 'You don't have... I'm not going to give you anything. Just forget it.'
So this [[Yemen|يمني]] man, now he's very upset, and he needs this money.
So he thinks, 'What should I do?'
So he decides to go to [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]]. Do we remember [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]]?
[[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]] was the meeting hall that was built by [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] many years earlier.

So the Yemeni man, he decided, "Okay, if I go to [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]], then I will find, you know, these big, important leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] there and I will complain to them and see what they do about it."

So he went to [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]], and he explained to those leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] that were gathered there the incident that happened to him with [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العَاص بن وَائِل]].
He told them, 'I sold him my goods. We agreed to a price. He told me to come back. He didn't give it to me.
He kept delaying it, and finally he said, "No, I'm not going to give you anything."'"
And it was the place where all of the important people of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] used to gather and discuss important affairs.
And then the [[Yemen|يمني]] man said to these people of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], 'If I don't get my right from this man, I will go around all of the [[Arab|عرب]] tribes,
So they would always be there, discussing different matters that were pertinent to their community and making decisions.
and I will tell them that the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] are dishonest in their business, they oppress the people who want to trade with them, they don't give the people their rights.
I will go around and I will destroy your reputation. I will destroy the reputation of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]
That was their place where they used to do these things. So the [[Yemen|يمني]] man, he decided, 'Okay, if I go to [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]],
then I will find, you know, these big, important leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] there, and I will complain to them and see what they do about it.'
if you don't get my right back from this man.'
So when they heard this, they actually got scared, because the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], living there in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]],
So he went to [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]],
and he explained to those leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] that were gathered there the incident that happened to him with [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص بن وائل]].

where do they get their income? All of their income is just from business, from trade. They don't have any agriculture there in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], they don't have any manufacturing in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], nothing.
All of their income, it was through trade.
So if their reputation was destroyed in this type of a way, that they're cheaters and they're deceivers and they take the money of the people,
if this happens to their reputation, then they will definitely lose out,
and their source of income would be destroyed. So they got scared.
So three of them stood up.
And the name of all three of these people who stood up, they all had the same name, the same first name: [[al-Fadl|الفضل]].
So three people, all of them named [[al-Fadl|الفضل]], [[al-Fadl|الفضل]], [[al-Fadl|الفضل]], they stood up, and they said,
they made an oath that we will fight whoever tries to oppress another, whoever takes the right of another person, we will fight him to the death.
We will fight him. If he returns the right of that person to the person who deserves it, then it's okay.
If he doesn't return it, then we will fight until either he is killed or we are killed.
So these three men named [[al-Fadl|الفضل]], they took this oath.
And that is how the name [[Hilf al-Fudul|حلف الفضول]] came.
The [[Hilf|حلف]] of [[Fudul|فضول]]. [[Fudul|فضول]] is the plural of [[al-Fadl|الفضل]].
And then they invited the other people, others to come and join them, take this oath with us.
So many of the people, they came and they took that oath of allegiance with them,
that, 'Yes, we will fight, not only for the rights of this [[Yemen|يمني]] man from [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص بن وائل]], but anyone, if any [[dhulm|ظلم]], if any oppression happens to anyone,
then we will not let that stand.
No matter who the oppressor is—he could be the most powerful of the people—we don't care.
If he has oppressed someone and taken the right of someone, we will fight him.
No matter who he is, and no matter how insignificant or low in status the person who is being oppressed is—it doesn't matter how poor he is, it doesn't matter how low his status is—we don't care.
If he is being wronged, if he is being oppressed, we will get his right back for him.'
So this was a very honorable oath that they took, and many of the people,
they took allegiance with that oath as well.
And the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], a young man, he also took this oath, and he said later on,

segments.text: He said, 'I was called to be part of an oath in the times of [[Jahiliyyah|جاهلية]] that even if I were to be called to the same type of oath in Islam, I would answer it, I would accept it.'
So it was an honorable oath.
And the Prophet ﷺ was part of that oath as well.
Again, Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] giving him this beautiful [[tarbiyah|تربية]],
being part of such a beautiful oath that shows honor, and that shows that you will fight for the rights of those who are weak.
For [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ being part of this from his young age, this is from the upbringing that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] caused him to have,
fighting for the rights of the downtrodden, of the poor, of the oppressed. And this was the way of the Prophet ﷺ throughout his life.
He would not stand for injustice. He would make sure that he fights for the rights of others,
whether they were Muslims or even non-Muslims. No non-Muslim would ever be wronged in front of [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ.
He would fight for the rights of everyone, and he would not allow anyone to be oppressed.
So the Prophet ﷺ witnessed, and he was part of [[Hilf al-Fudul|حلف الفضول]] as well.
So when they took this oath, these people in [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]], and many people joined them,
they went straight to the house of [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص بن وائل]]. They went straight to his house with their swords taken out.
And they took this [[Yemen|يمني]] guy with them, said, "We're going to get your right back for you, don't worry. Come with us."
So a bunch of them, all these big people from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], with their swords in their hands, to the house of [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص بن وائل]].
They knock his door. He opens the door, and look at the sight! All of these guys with swords, and the [[Yemen|يمني]] poor guy is with them.
And they say to [[al-As ibn Wa'il|العاص]], "You will return the right of this man, or you will be killed right now. Your choice: return it to him, or die."
So he was surprised. "You're saying you're going to kill me? Do you know who I am? I am this big leader from the leaders of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
You will kill me for not giving the money to this poor [[Yemen|يمني]] guy? Who is he?"
And they said, "We have made an oath that we will fight for the rights of those who are wronged and oppressed.
And if you don't do as we are saying, then all you have is the sword."
So when he saw how serious they were, that they weren't kidding around, he got scared and he actually returned the money of that [[Yemen|يمني]] man to him.
This was [[Hilf al-Fudul|حلف الفضول]], very honorable oath that these people took.
And when Islam came, this oath was not canceled. It remained throughout the time of Islam.
It remained throughout the time of the [[Sahabah|صحابة]], through the time of the Khulafa al-Rashidin.
Al-[[Hassan|حسان]] or Al-[[Husayn|الحسين]] [[radiyallahu 'anhu|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ]], once he was oppressed by one of the rulers in [[Madinah|مدينة]],
and he wanted to get his right back from that man, his name was Al-Walid.
And Al-Walid would not give the right of Al-[[Husayn|الحسين]] to him. So Al-[[Husayn|الحسين]] said to him,

segments.translit: La-tu'idanna ilayya haqqi wa illa nadaytu bi-Hilfil-Fudul.

segments.text: He said to Al-Walid, "Either you will give me back my right, or I will call out with [[Hilf al-Fudul|حلف الفضول]]."
And [[Abdullah ibn Zubayr|عبد الله بن الزبير]], he heard this, the great صحابي [[Abdullah ibn Zubayr|عبد الله بن الزبير]].
And he said, "[[Wallahi|والله]], I swear by Allah, if he calls out with [[Hilf al-Fudul|حلف الفضول]],
then I will take out my sword and I will fight with my sword until his right is returned to him, or I am killed fighting for his right."
So this [[Hilf al-Fudul|حلف الفضول]], beautiful oath that they took,
yes, it was made in the time of [[Jahiliyyah|جاهلية]], but it lasted throughout the time of Islam, and it lasted through the time of the [[Sahabah|صحابة]] and the Khulafa al-Rashidin,
and it lasted all the way into al-Dawlah al-Umawiyyah,
because of the principles that it was based upon. And the principles that it was based upon, they were consistent with the principles of Islam.
And that is why it remained throughout Islam.
So the Prophet ﷺ, he was part of this and he witnessed this.
And again, this is from the way that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] caused him to be raised so that
he would be ready for his role as the Messenger of Allah when that time was to come.
Now, when the Prophet ﷺ turned 25,
so he's still a young man, 25 years old,
then a very great event happened in his life.
And you know that it was 25 years old when he married [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة بنت خويلد]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]].
So what is the background of the marriage of the Prophet ﷺ to [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]]?
[[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], she was a very honorable woman.
And she was from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] as well. And she was very, very, very rich. Not just rich, but very, very, very rich.
And she was also from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]. She was from the lineage of [[Abd al-Uzza ibn Qusayy ibn Kilab|عبد العزى بن قصي بن كلاب]].
The Prophet ﷺ, his lineage traces back to [[Abd Manaf ibn Qusayy ibn Kilab|عبد مناف بن قصي بن كلاب]],
and [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]], she traces back to [[Abd al-Uzza ibn Qusayy ibn Kilab|عبد العزى بن قصي بن كلاب]].
So they were both from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], both from a very honorable background and lineage.
And [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], she was
very honorable and respected amongst the people, and she was very, very rich. It was said that her wealth
was equivalent to the wealth of the rest of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].

If you took the rest of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] and you added all the wealth that they had, it was equivalent to the wealth that [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]] had herself.
So that's how rich she was.
But still, even though she was so rich, she was of the utmost honor and respect, and she had the best character.
Now, [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], she had been married before, and her husband died.
And then she married again, and her second husband also died. So she was widowed twice.
And she used to do business, but as a woman,
she could not take these business trips that the businessmen would take, you know, going from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to [[Sham|شام]], going to [[Yemen|اليمن]] and going to these places to do trade.
As a woman, she couldn't do this type of a thing because
there were a lot of dangers on the ways, right? There were these highway robbers, and there were criminals, and these types of things.
So it was not suitable for a woman to go and do business by herself.
So what [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]] would do to keep doing business is that she would hire some of the men of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]
to go and do business on her behalf, to make these trips, to do this travel
with her goods and sell it, and do business on her behalf. And then she would give them
either a fixed sum that they had agreed upon, or she would give them some percentage of the profits. So this is the way that she would do business.
So not all of these men who were doing business on her behalf, not all of them were trustworthy.
You know, some of them were dishonest, some of them, you know, didn't do the business in the right way.
And she knew that. She knew that, you know, there are some people who are maybe more trustworthy, some people who are less trustworthy. So she wanted to find someone
who she could trust 100%, who would be 100% sincere and trustworthy to do business on her behalf. Someone she could trust
without having any question.
And of course, the reputation of [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ was there.
He was known as [[al-Sadiq al-Amin|الصادق الأمين]]. He was known as the truthful one, the trustworthy one.
He was known as someone who never lied, someone who never cheated, someone who never deceived others,
someone who never even spoke in a bad way. He never even spoke with vulgar or obscene words.
So he had the perfect character, and nobody could say anything bad about him.
Everything about him was good, and he was known for this. So [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], she knew about this as well.
So she called for him and she spoke to him, and she told him that, "I would like you to do business on my behalf."
And he agreed. He said, "Okay, I will do it for you."
So he set out to do business with the wealth of [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]] to [[Sham|شام]], the greater Syria area.
That is where they used to go to do a lot of business, the people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]]...
[[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], she sent her slave, his name was [[Maysarah|ميسرة]].
She sent him to accompany [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ on this journey.
Because [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] had made this trip many times before,
and he knew the way very well, and he knew the people in [[Sham|شَام]], the businessmen in [[Sham|شَام]] very well,
so he could introduce [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ to these people,
because this was his first trip that he was taking.
So [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]] decided to send [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] to accompany [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ.
So they start their journey,
and [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] is amazed from the beginning
at the [[akhlaq|أَخْلَاق]], the character, the beautiful manners of [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ.
He is so humble. He is from such a lineage,
he is from the lineage of the leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]],
yet still, he would sit with this slave, sit with [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] and eat with him and talk with him.
You know, not make [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] feel inferior to him.
And this was something that he, the slave, [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] found very strange, because usually people who are powerful,
or who come from a respectable family,
they don't deal with slaves like this.
You know, they will make sure that the slave knows his place.
But [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ was different. He would sit with him, talk with him, eat with him.
So he noticed this.
Another thing that he noticed was
on their way to [[Sham|الشَّام]],
they were always under the shade of a cloud. Just like
the first time when the Prophet ﷺ, when he was 12 years old and he went with his uncle [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], a cloud was
covering them so the heat of the sun would not harm them, the same thing happened again.
So [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] and [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, they're on the way and a cloud is following them the whole way.
While they were on their way,
they passed by that same monastery that they had passed by years earlier,
that we spoke about last week. But by this time, the head monk of that monastery, [[Buhayra|بحيرى]], he had passed away. He was not alive anymore.
And there was a new monk who was in charge of that monastery.
And he witnessed [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] and [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ coming in this small caravan,
and he noticed, just like [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] had noticed years earlier, he noticed the cloud
following them as well.
So they took a stop to rest in that area nearby the monastery.
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ told [[Maysarah|ميسرة]], "You stay here with the caravan.
I'm just going to go off a little bit."
So he went off,
a little bit off the path and he found a tree,
and he rested under that tree. [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, he rested under that tree.
And this monk from the monastery, he's noticing all of this. He's watching it.
So he runs to [[Maysarah|ميسرة]],
and he said, "I noticed something very, very amazing with your caravan."
And then [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] said, "What is it?"
He said, "I noticed that a cloud
was covering you as you were coming along." And then [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] said, "Yeah, I noticed that too. That's strange, huh?"
And then the monk said, "And I noticed something else, too.
The man that you are with, he went and he's resting under that tree."
Now [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] was confused here. He didn't think this is anything special. So what? Okay, he went and he's resting under that tree. What's the big deal about that?
And then this Christian monk says, "In our revelation, in our scriptures, that tree,
nobody would sit and rest under that tree except a prophet."
So now [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] is amazed. He's like, "Wow, really?" He said, "Yes.
This is something special."
So now, throughout the rest of their journey up to [[Sham|الشَّام]] and in [[Sham|شَام]], [[Maysarah|ميسرة]],
the slave of [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]],
is keeping a very close focus on everything that [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ does.
Because now that he has this information,
he wants to keep a close eye on everything that he's doing.
And he notices
there in [[Sham|الشَّام]]
the beautiful manners and the honesty of the Prophet ﷺ. He also notices that he's very good in what he's doing.
That he's very good in this trade, in this business.
He's excellent, and he's honest,
and he's kind, and he's compassionate. If he's dealing with someone
who is poor,
he still makes sure that he deals with them
in a beautiful way.
He doesn't take advantage of anyone, even when it's easy to do so. He makes sure that everything is done with complete honesty.
So [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] is noticing all of these characteristics, the beautiful way that the Prophet ﷺ is dealing with everyone.
And another thing that shows the smart business sense that the Prophet ﷺ had
is that he sold [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]]'s goods in [[Sham|الشَّام]],
and then he bought goods from [[Sham|شَام]] to go back and sell in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. And this was not the way that the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] used to do business.
Rather, they would take the goods from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and they would go sell it in [[Sham|شَام]] and come back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] with the profits.
But [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ,
he did that, but then he also bought goods from [[Sham|شَام]],
and when he came back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], he sold all of that in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] as well.
So he made the profits twice.

He made profit in [[Sham|الشَّام]], and then he made profit in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] as well. So [[Maysarah|ميسرة]] is noticing all of these things, saying, "Hey, that's actually a very smart thing to do.
No one used to do that before."
So when
he comes back to [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], he gives her all of the profits that he made.
And it is the most profit that she ever made from any of these trips with the other people.
Those other people that she would send to do business on her behalf, maybe they wouldn't even come with 10% of what he came back with.
So she was amazed. It was much more than what she expected.
So she saw that this is something amazing and there is so much [[barakah|بَرَكَة]] and blessing in the work of this man.
And then [[Maysarah|ميسرة]]
also told her everything about what he saw accompanying him on this trip.
He told her about his humility, his kindness, his compassion, his honesty,
the way that he deals with poor people, the way that he deals
with weak people, everything is 100% perfect.
This is the perfect man.
So [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]] was very impressed with this,
and her heart grew attached to [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ,
and she was interested in marrying him. She was interested to marry him.
He had everything, right? He had this character, he had
honesty, he had sincerity, and it was proven to her by this. So she wanted to marry him. But
she was not sure how it could be arranged. Because like we mentioned before,
she was
40 years old, and she was married and widowed twice before.
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ was 25 years old, and he had never been married before.
So there was that.
So she spoke to
a woman named [[Nafisah|نفيسة]]
to go to [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ and just get an idea
if he would be interested in marrying her.
So she sent this woman, [[Nafisah|نفيسة]], to speak on her behalf to [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ to get an idea if he would be interested in
marrying her.
So [[Nafisah|نفيسة]], she went to [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ,
and she asked him, "[[Ya|يَا]] [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]], why don't you get married?"
He was 25 years old at this time,
and the habit of the Arabs at that time is that they would get married early.
You know, they would get married maybe 16 or 17 years old.
But he was 25 years old and he hadn't gotten married yet. So she asked him, "Why don't you get married? Why haven't you gotten married?" And he said, "Because I'm not...
I don't have wealth."
As we mentioned, the Prophet ﷺ was poor.
So he said, "Because I don't... I'm not wealthy. I don't have money. How can I get married?"
And then she said
to him, "What if there is someone that you can marry who is
beautiful, and she's from a great lineage, and she's honorable, and she's trustworthy, and she's also very rich? Would you be interested in marrying her?
If she wants to marry you, would you be interested in marrying her?"
And he said, "Who are you talking about?"
And then she said, "[[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة بنت خُوَيْلِد]]."
And then the Prophet ﷺ said, "[[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]]? She would want to marry me?"
The reason why he was surprised
was because
[[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] had received many, many proposals from people.
She was beautiful and she was from a respectable lineage and she was rich. She had everything going for her.
So even though she was widowed twice,
after that, she still was receiving many, many proposals from different men, and she was refusing all of them.
She was refusing everyone.
So [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ was surprised when [[Nafisah|نفيسة]] suggested this.
He said, "[[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]]? [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] would want to marry me?"
And then [[Nafisah|نفيسة]] said, "Don't worry about it. I will set everything up.
I will set everything up."
And she did set it up, and they did get married, and it turned out to be the most successful, most beautiful marriage.
And [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], next week we will talk more about the marriage of [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ to [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] and their children and their family life.
